knowledge:
- key_parameters: width=Width of the output Circos plot in pixels ;; height=Height of the output Circos plot in pixels ;; zoom=Logical value (TRUE/FALSE) indicating whether to enable zooming on the plot ;; genome=A named list specifying the chromosomes/scaffolds and their respective lengths ;; genomeFillColor=Character vector of colors or a predefined color palette name (e.g., "Blues") to fill the genome tracks ;; moduleList=A track or combination of tracks (concatenated using '+') to be displayed on the Circos plot ;; minRadius=The inner radius of a specific track module ;; maxRadius=The outer radius of a specific track module ;; data=The input data frame containing genomic coordinates and values for the track
- alternatives: circosJS or BioCircos.js native JavaScript libraries which require local installation, compiling extra libraries, or manual data processing ;; static Circos plotting packages in R (such as circlize) when interactive web-based features are not required
- when_to_use: When you need to visualize multi-dimensional genomic data (such as SNPs, copy number variations, expression data, or genomic interactions) in an interactive, web-friendly circular layout
- pitfalls: Failing to match the chromosome/scaffold names in the track data with the names defined in the genome list parameter ;; Overlapping tracks by setting conflicting minRadius and maxRadius values across different modules

workflows.name: interactive_circos_histogram
workflows.intent: Create an interactive Circos plot displaying a genomic histogram track.
input: histogram_data.csv (Data frame containing genomic coordinates and values for the histogram track)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the interacCircos library ;; 2. Load the histogram data ;; 3. Generate the interactive Circos plot with CircosHistogram and Circos
workflows.code:
library(interacCircos)

histogramData <- histogramExample
Circos(moduleList=CircosHistogram('HISTOGRAM01', data = histogramData,
      fillColor= "#ff7f0e",maxRadius = 210,minRadius = 175,
      animationDisplay = TRUE),genome=list("2L"=23011544,"2R"=21146708,"3L"=24543557,"3R"= 27905053,"X"=22422827,"4"=1351857),
      outerRadius = 220, width = 700,height = 550)

workflows.name: interactive_circos_snp_background
workflows.intent: Create an interactive Circos plot displaying SNP data points overlaid on a background track.
input: snp_data.csv (Data frame containing SNP coordinates and values)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the interacCircos library ;; 2. Load the SNP data ;; 3. Combine the SNP track and background track using the plus operator ;; 4. Generate the interactive Circos plot using Circos
workflows.code:
library(interacCircos)

snpData <- snpExample
Circos(moduleList=CircosSnp('SNP01', minRadius =150, 
      maxRadius = 190, data = snpExample,SNPFillColor= "#9ACD32", 
      circleSize= 2, SNPAxisColor= "#B8B8B8", SNPAxisWidth= 0.5, 
      animationDisplay=TRUE,animationTime= 2000, animationDelay= 0, 
      animationType= "linear") + 
      CircosBackground('BG01',minRadius = 145,maxRadius = 200),
      width = 700,height = 550)
